configs.name: f32_clean
configs.note: low-noise: the only configuration where LoopCD-Hidden is meaningful. ctx is small on purpose: f32 KV is 4 bytes/value, so a 4096 ctx would need ~13 GB of KV on top of the 10 GB model.

configs.name: shipping
configs.note: shipping stack; LoopCD-Hidden degenerates here (M3 finding)

configs.name: shipping_r2
configs.note: shipping stack at half the recurrent depth (R=2 instead of R=4) - the paper's compute-saving regime, where LoopCD is meant to recover the accuracy lost to the halving

configs.name: kitty_shipping
configs.note: M6 Kitty-KV 2-bit cache on the shipping stack. ctx 2048, NOT 4096: M6 stores f16 (the 2-bit win is M7), so one K/V tensor at ctx 4096 is 3.00 GiB and the Vulkan driver rejects a single allocation of that size (ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory); at ctx 2048 it is 1.5 GiB and fits. Default kernel flags: sink 32, page 128, boost 0.25, kbits/vbits 2, boost_bits 4.

configs.name: kitty_clean
configs.note: M6 Kitty-KV on f32 weights + CPU. The low-noise condition; slow (~1 tok/s), so it is run with a reduced condition set.

configs.name: kitty_packed_shipping
configs.note: M7 packed 2-bit cache on the shipping stack, ctx 4096 (attempt 8192). Same boost count as kitty_shipping. Compare same-ctx only.
